subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this generalized durable runtime, persistent schema, and public Gateway/CLI/plugin-SDK surface as core architecture for the release line?
rationale: The patch is a broad architectural and product commitment that crosses persistence, agent lifecycle, Gateway protocol, plugin SDK, CLI, and release operations; repository policy and VISION.md do not make that direction automatic.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed stack
options.body: Approve the architecture in principle, then require a current-main, issue-linked sequence with minimal public surface and complete upgrade/runtime proof.

options.title: Sponsor the cumulative branch
options.body: Accept the broad release-branch stack after fixing the dependency pin and supplying exact-head runtime and upgrade evidence.

options.title: Decline core durable architecture
options.body: Keep the existing session-delivery queue and close the durable stack unless a narrower concrete core gap is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed stack
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture in principle, then require a current-main, issue-linked sequence with minimal public surface and complete upgrade/runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sets core architecture and release direction beyond the ownership of any single runtime file.
